If it's over 30%, this could indicate Kahf Guard is using more battery than expected. Otherwise, the issue might be due to other factors.

If you use apps like Facebook, Instagram, or YouTube for extended periods, Kahf Guard will also run longer to protect you, which may consume more battery. Therefore, compared to apps that you use only occasionally, Kahf Guard may use slightly more battery.

safe_internet_review_3_quote: Khaf Guard has helped me build healthier digital habits. I use it to block Facebook Reels, YouTube Shorts, and Instagram Reels, which were silently consuming a lot of my time. After blocking them, my focus and productivity improved noticeably. My wife and I both use the app and share account access to see each other's screen time, which creates accountability and encourages more mindful phone usage. Simple, practical, and very useful.
